subject: Clarify CloudCart marketplace pass-through, data residency scope, and liability for order form
messages:
From: Gavin Ortiz <gavin@cloudcart.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudcart.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:23:12 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum — pass-through liability & data residency questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the draft marketplace addendum last week. Procurement reviewed it and we have two principal items blocking approval on our side:

1) Pass-through liability: the addendum currently references an indemnity carve-out that would cascade liabilities to CloudCart for customer claims arising from downstream integrations. Our legal team needs the language tightened so liability is limited to amounts actually invoiced through the marketplace (no consequential carve-through). Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to narrow the pass-through?

2) Data residency/scope: the Order Form references the marketplace listing but isn’t explicit about where account-level customer data will reside when transacted via CloudCart (EU customers in particular). We need an explicit commitment or a reference to a schedule that lists regionals available. If Redwood can point to a binding scope we can close faster.

If you can send a redlined addendum and an estimate of how long your legal ops needs to finalize, procurement can queue the DocuSign. We’re hoping for signature within 4 business days if possible.

Appreciate the help — Gavin
Gavin Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, CloudCart

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Gavin Ortiz <gavin@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:09:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — pass-through liability & data residency questions

Gavin — thanks for the clear summary.

Attached: Redwood_Marketplace_Addendum_v2.docx (redlines included). I also attached a short spreadsheet with the current region mapping for marketplace-hosted instances (CloudCart note: CloudCart-specific routing not yet committed in an SLA).

Short answers up front:
- Liability/pass-through: we can narrow the pass-through to apply only to direct invoiced SaaS fees collected via CloudCart (we propose an explicit cap equal to the invoiced amount plus direct remediation costs). See section 7.2 in the redline.
- Data residency: we cannot blanket-guarantee EU-only residency for third-party integrations at the marketplace level; however, we can include an optional schedule that binds residency commitments per Order Form (see Schedule A placeholder). For EU customers we can offer routing to our EU tenancy for the listed products — pending capacity and formal order form election.

Next steps / timelines:
- Laura: can you review the liability cap language and confirm ops can support the per-order residency election by EOD Thu (6/17)?
- Ben: can you confirm the commercial ask (any required offset to price if we offer EU tenancy) so procurement has the correct economics?
- Gavin: if the redline looks OK I’ll update and request a final sign-from-Redwood DocuSign link.

(attachment: Redwood_Marketplace_Addendum_v2.docx - 145 KB)
(attachment: CloudCart_DataResidency_Specs.xlsx - 32 KB)

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Gavin Ortiz <gavin@cloudcart.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:36:20 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — pass-through liability & data residency questions

On Tue, Jun 14, 2027 at 11:09 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached: Redwood_Marketplace_Addendum_v2.docx (redlines included).

Thanks Soojin — quick internal notes:
- From a sales perspective we want to avoid long carveouts that increase our legal/ops burden. Narrowing to invoiced amounts + remediation makes sense as a commercial compromise.
- On data residency, CloudCart will push hard for EU assurance. If we make the residency election per-Order-Form, we should bake a simple checkbox and rate card for EU tenancy so sales can quote it cleanly. Laura — can ops instrument this in the onboarding flow?

Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Director, Revenue Operations

> Laura: can you review the liability cap language and confirm ops can support the per-order residency election by EOD Thu (6/17)?

Laura here — short answer: yes, we can support the per-order residency election but need these two clarifications in the addendum: 1) an onboarding window (30 days) for tenancy provisioning, and 2) a failover policy if capacity is unavailable (auto-fallback to hosted region with notice). I added suggested text below that might fit into section 3 (data routing):

"Residency election: Customer may elect EU tenancy via Order Form. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provision EU tenancy within thirty (30) days of Order Form execution. If Redwood cannot provision EU tenancy within such window, Redwood will notify Customer and provide the option to (a) accept temporary hosting in Redwood's US tenancy for up to sixty (60) days with pro-rated credit, or (b) terminate the applicable Order Form without penalty."

I pasted the clause into the redline. Ben — we should confirm whether the 30/60 days and credit are acceptable to CloudCart (procurement).

Ben

From: Gavin Ortiz <gavin@cloudcart.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudcart.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:02:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — pass-through liability & data residency questions

Soojin / Ben / Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity. Procurement reviewed the redline and the proposed liability cap is acceptable in principle. A couple of small asks before we sign:

- Please replace "pro-rated credit" language with an explicit formula (we propose: daily rate = monthly subscription fee / 30; credit = number of days of temporary hosting * daily rate).
- For the EU tenancy provisioning window, CloudCart requests a one-time exception: if an Order Form is executed for >5,000 EU MAUs we need a 45-day provisioning window (we can mark this in the Order Form when applicable).

If you can update those two bullets and resend the final addendum I’ll route to our CFO for DocuSign the same day. If you prefer, attach a final PDF and I can sign immediately.

Thanks — Gavin
(Procurement: procurement@cloudcart.com)
